# The `sp` command line

Every command Scripture Pipelines provides, and the contract behind the three that write
into your project. The CLI is `sp` — `llmflow run` and `llmflow lint` are stale and will
not work.

`tests/test_cli_is_documented.py` fails when the CLI gains a command this file does not
name, so the list below cannot quietly fall behind the program.

## Keeping a project current

**Run either `sp doctor` or `sp init --update` and you have an up-to-date environment.**
They differ in exactly one thing, named below.

| | creates a project that has nothing | restores what is missing or has drifted | writes the starter examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sp init` | yes | yes | yes |
| `sp init --update` | no | yes | refreshes one that is present |
| `sp doctor` | no | yes | never |

The starter examples — `pipelines/hello.yaml`, `pipelines/hello-llmflow.yaml`,
`prompts/hello.gpt`, `prompts/reply.gpt` — are the whole difference. A project that
deleted them has decided something, and re-creating them would overrule it. Everything
else sp owns comes back whether it was deleted, corrupted or never installed.

**`sp doctor` is not read-only.** It overwrites a `generated` file that has drifted.
Commit or stash before running it.

### What sp owns, and what it will never touch

Ownership is declared in `data/file-catalog.yaml`, one row per path, and read from there
by every command. It is not a rule written down anywhere else, and a file's location does
not decide it.

| policy | meaning |
|---|---|
| `generated` | sp owns the content. Restored when missing and when it has drifted. |
| `create-once` | sp writes it when absent, then never again. It is yours. |
| `example` | `sp init` creates it; `sp init --update` refreshes one that is present; `sp doctor` leaves it alone. |
| `user-owned` | sp never writes it. |

Two consequences worth knowing before running anything:

- **`docs/ai-context/sp/` is `generated`.** An edit there is lost on the next run. Change
  the file it came from — a template under `src/llmflow/templates/`, or a constant — and
  the change reaches every project rather than one.
- **`docs/ai-context/project/`, `CLAUDE.md` and `project/` are yours.** Written once if
  absent and never rewritten. Whatever you put in them survives every command here.

### The failure this arrangement exists to prevent

A skill added to Scripture Pipelines after a project was set up does not appear in that
project by itself, and until 2026-09-19 nothing said so: `sp doctor` asked whether the
project could see *any* skills rather than all of them, and reported a project holding ten
of eleven as complete. Two projects sat in that state.

So: **a green report means every catalogued file is present and matches what this
installation ships** — not that the project once installed correctly. Anything absent is
written and named in the report, `.claude/skills/` included, which is the directory Claude
Code actually reads. `~/.sp/skills/` is Scripture Pipelines' own store and is not a
location any assistant reads; a skill that reaches only there is not invocable.

## Running pipelines

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| `sp run` | Run a pipeline. Takes `--pipeline`, `--var key=value`, `--dry-run`, `--rewind-to`. **Calls LLMs and costs money** — never run one without being asked. |
| `sp lint` | Validate a pipeline without executing it. |
| `sp list` | List available pipelines. |
| `sp clean` | Delete the contents of the declared `intermediate_file_directory`. It cannot reach the deliverable. |
| `sp tools replay` | Test a prompt change against captured debug requests, cheaply. |

## Setting up this machine

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| `sp init` | Create a starter environment. `--update` refreshes, `--no-examples` skips the starter files. |
| `sp doctor` | Check this machine's setup and restore any file sp owns that is missing or has drifted. |
| `sp setup` | Configure AI provider API keys. |
| `sp models` | List available models by provider. |
| `sp version` | Show the version. |

## Data this machine can read

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| `sp resource list` | The texts this machine can open, and their status. |
| `sp resource add` | Register a resource so pipelines can name it. |
| `sp resource set` | Set fields on a registration, leaving the rest alone. |
| `sp dataset list` | Datasets registered on this machine. |
| `sp dataset add` | Record where a dataset lives on this machine. |
| `sp dataset search` | Search the whole catalog, not only what is readable. |
| `sp dataset download` | Fetch a dataset without registering a resource. |
| `sp load-db` | Load a downloaded dataset into a database (basex, …). |

**`sp resource list` shows only what is readable here.** To find something the catalog
knows about but this machine has not got, use `sp dataset search`.

## The global registry and AI context

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| `sp registry list` | List registered resources. |
| `sp registry info` | Show detailed information about a resource. |
| `sp registry status` | Show registry status and location. |
| `sp registry context` | Generate AI context from the registry. |
| `sp context list` | List available AI context files. |
| `sp context add` | Register an AI context file in the global registry. |
| `sp context search` | Search the AI context registry by topic. |
| `sp update-ai-context` | Regenerate the `docs/ai-context/` helper files. |

## Content lifecycle

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| `sp content status` | Show content status across stages. |
| `sp content list` | List all files in a stage. |
| `sp content diff` | Compare content versions across stages. |
| `sp content gui` | Launch the web-based content management GUI. |
| `sp transition` | Move content between lifecycle stages. |
| `sp gui` | Launch the web-based GUI. |
